---
title: "simstim policy lockdown"
---

<!-- Generated by `just docs` from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Pause session allowances and refuse unknown network destinations.

```text
simstim policy lockdown [flags]
```

Applies the locked preset and refuses unknown destinations on every reached sandbox. Session allowances pause; session denies and broader rules remain. Refused open flows close. The host keeps the restriction for later starts, including starts from another laptop. `--off` removes only this restriction and needs the literal word lockdown. It applies no local policy edits and fetches no credentials. Unreached hosts stay pending and make this command fail.

## Examples

```sh
simstim policy lockdown
simstim policy lockdown --host my-vps
simstim policy lockdown --off --confirm=lockdown
```

## Flags

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--confirm <string>` | the literal word lockdown, required with `--off` when input is off |
| `--host <string>` | change lockdown on this saved host only |
| `--json` | print JSON for scripts, and ask nothing (see docs/how-to/scripting.md) |
| `--off` | lift only the lockdown restriction |

## Flags from the parent command

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--debug[=<categories>]` | turn on the debug mode, with every category, or with the categories listed: attach, net, memory, launcher, runtime. A list binds only in the = form, such as `--debug=net` |
| `--debug-file <file>` | write the client's debug records to this file. On its own, it turns on every category (SIMSTIM_DEBUG_FILE does the same) |
| `--no-color` | print no colour (NO_COLOR does the same) |
| `--no-input` | ask nothing: a question that needs an answer fails with exit code 4, and names the flag that answers it (SIMSTIM_NO_INPUT=1 does the same) |

Part of [`policy`](policy.md): read and change sandbox policy at any layer.
